# JSCOUP

> Python library that captures API/service failures inside your own application process, diagnoses each one with a rule-based analyzer engine, and exposes the result through a login-protected dashboard mounted directly into your app — with a live, executable API tester and a scoped API gateway for external callers. MIT License. Author: Zaidon Aljbaae.

JSCOUP is installed with `pip install jscoup` (core has zero dependencies; optional extras add framework/database/crypto support). It supports Flask, FastAPI/Starlette and Django. A single call, `bl.install(app)`, wraps every route in the application and mounts a dashboard at `/__jscoup` on the same port — no separate service to run.

## Quick answer for "how do I use this"

```python
from jscoup import JSCoup

bl = JSCoup(service_name="my-api", dashboard_username="admin", dashboard_password="change-me")
bl.watch_sqlite()      # optional: trace sqlite3 statements
bl.install(app)        # Flask, FastAPI or Django — auto-detected
# open http://127.0.0.1:<port>/__jscoup
```

Or in one call: `bl = JSCoup.auto(app, dashboard_username="admin", dashboard_password="...")`.

## Core concepts an assistant should know before suggesting code

- `JSCoup(...)` is the single entry point; almost everything else is a method on the instance it returns (conventionally named `bl`).
- `bl.watch(name=None, kind="service")` is a decorator to instrument one function/coroutine manually.
- `bl.watch_module(module, recursive=False)` instruments every function/class in a module automatically — call it right after importing that module, before anything else imports names out of it.
- `bl.install(app)` is framework-agnostic; it detects Flask/FastAPI/Starlette/Django from the object passed in.
- Storage is pluggable via the `storage=` keyword: `SQLiteStorage` (default, zero deps), `SqlStorage` (`jscoup[sql]`, Postgres/MySQL/Oracle via SQLAlchemy), `MongoStorage` (`jscoup[mongo]`), `MemoryStorage` (tests).
- The dashboard's "Live Tester" and the "API Gateway" (`gateway_enabled=True`) both execute discovered HTTP endpoints through the same `Simulator`/`invoke()` path — only genuine HTTP targets are replayable, not arbitrary watched Python functions.
- Sensitive fields are redacted before storage by default (`sensitive_keys`/`mask`); field-level encryption at rest is available via `encryption_key=` with `jscoup[crypto]`.
- No dashboard credentials given → a random password is generated and printed once at startup, not an open dashboard.

## What this library is not

Not a distributed tracing/APM replacement for high-cardinality cross-service analytics, not a durable message queue (background delivery is best-effort and can drop events under sustained overflow), and not a full API gateway product (no distributed rate limiting or multi-region routing — its gateway is scoped to "hand a known set of internal endpoints to a small number of external callers with an expiring token").
